q1_issues.issue: The bare kind 'cancer' is used as a constant Agent filler of a single unmarked event, but the instruction set licenses the bare class symbol only for a non-specific/generic OBJECT and routes a bare-kind subject with a habitual present predicate into the verbal-generic Implication rule form.

q2_gaps: Population-level / aggregate statistical generic with a bare-kind (mass) subject — 'Cancer kills thousands of people every year': the kind-relation route is blocked because the object is a quantified NP rather than a bare kind, and the prescribed per-instance Implication rule would falsely assert that each instance of the kind kills thousands per year, so neither licensed route expresses an annual-incidence claim.

Per-member distribution of a predicate onto a group filling a non-subject (Patient) role — the distributive-rule machinery is stated only for members that act (bark, pass, laugh, arrive) and for group subjects, so it is undefined whether the killed group also takes a PartOf rule.
notes: The vague-count encoding (GroupOf + CardinalityPhrase "thousands", no partitive since it is 'of people' not 'of the people'), the Patient role for a destroying verb, the absence of a tense atom, and (Every e 1 year) for the periodic 'every year' are all correct. All atoms carry the default (STV 1.0 0.99) although the claim is an empirical generalization, but the instruction set's confidence dial is written for Inheritance generics and rules rather than habitual event bundles, so I have not counted that as a defect.
